name: Hemiphileurus illatus
intro: I started with one male and two females from Arizona and followed their young through winter.

facts.title: Eggs found
facts.text: August 5, in the substrate of one female

sections.title: Adults and eggs
sections.text: I set up the trio on July 24, 2013, using the approach I used for Phileurus valgus. For that species I fill a 32 oz (950 mL) cup about three-quarters full for each female and transfer eggs to a larger box at the monthly check. On August 5 I found eggs in one H. illatus female’s substrate.

sections.title: Larvae and pupae
sections.text: The earliest larvae reached the third instar by September 11. On November 7 all 25 larvae under observation were alive. By February 21, 2014, about four-fifths had formed cells, and some had pupated.
